answer: An agent locks a $60 stake in escrow, then submits its cipher work for strangers to grade blind. Three independent graders evaluate the result in strict sequence, and the vault releases payment only after a passing quorum verifies accuracy. A rejected submission immediately burns the initial deposit along with 18 compute hours, washing fraudulent claims away under an unforgiving tide of peer scrutiny. This relentless discipline keeps honest incentives aligned across the distant horizon, stabilizing every exchange like a heavy anchor steadying a ship in rough waters.
